stem: Why does WCAG 2.1 require alternative text for meaningful non-text elements such as photographs and informative diagrams?

options.text: Because the alternative text is displayed as a visible caption beneath each image.
options.shortLabel: Alt text shown as a visible caption
options.rationale: Captions are visible text added to the page; alternative text is exposed to assistive technology and is not displayed as a caption.

options.text: Because WCAG applies text equivalents to images of text but not to photographs.
options.shortLabel: Equivalents for images of text, not photos
options.rationale: The requirement covers all meaningful non-text content, including photographs and diagrams, not only images of text.

options.text: Because text can be converted into speech, braille, or enlarged print.
options.shortLabel: Text renders across speech, braille, and print
options.rationale: Text is universally adaptable; assistive technologies can convert text into speech, tactile braille, or magnified fonts.

options.text: Because a text alternative lets the image be enlarged without pixelation.
options.rationale: Enlargement is handled by the image format or the browser, not by a text alternative.

explanation: Text is a flexible medium in information technology. A text alternative lets user agents present the same information as speech, braille, or enlarged text, so the content is available in whichever form the user needs.

references.title: WCAG 2.1 Understanding Docs: Understanding SC 1.1.1 Non-text Content
